title: NBA instructs sportsbook partners to ban certain bets ripe for manipulation, per report - CBS Sports
description: Notably, 'under' parlays on the same player's statistics are off the board
body:
Notably, 'under' parlays on the same player's statistics are off the board
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the aftermath of multiple high-profile gambling scandals, the NBA will no longer allow certain types of bets that would appear to be the lowest-hanging fruit for potential conspirators. Citing a memo distributed to the league's sportsbook partners on Friday, ESPN is reporting that "bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays, in addition to other betting markets the league considers problematic."
From ESPN: The league also directed its authorized gambling operators, including DraftKings and FanDuel, not to offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.The NBA has the authority to restrict what partner sportsbooks offer through its agreements. The NBA estimates its partner sportsbooks account for upward of 99% of the U.S. betting market.These bets on an individual player's over/under lines are particularly ripe for fixing because the player can control the outcome. These were the bets exploited by Jontay Porter, who received a lifetime ban in 2024 for disclosing inside information to bettors and wagering on games. Porter admitted in court that he took himself out of games early to make sure his under bets hit. 
If you're not familiar with how these lines work, let's say a player's rebounding line for a game is set at 3.5. If you bet the under, you are betting that the player will finish with three or fewer rebounds. Obviously, a player can largely control that by simply not pursuing rebounds, and he can eliminate the possibility of even accidentally running into a loose rebound or two by simply removing himself from the game for a fake injury once he has logged the time to make the game and bets on his lines official. He relays this information to bettors beforehand, and they put a bunch of money on him to go under the projected total. ESPN notes that in the Porter criminal complaint, federal prosecutors pointed to one bettor placing an $80,000 parlay bet on Porter going under his line for assists, rebounds, points, 3-pointers, steals and blocks for a March 2024 game between the Raptors and Kings that stood to pay out more than a million dollars. Porter left that game after playing just three minutes. The same type of scandal has been alleged involving Terry Rozier, who removed himself after playing just nine minutes in a 2023 game that was called into question for the same conspiratorial reasons, and Malik Beasley. 
The NBA knows how bad a look this is for a league now so deeply connected with gaming partners, and these measures are a clear indication that it is trying, to whatever extent possible, to put the genie back in the bottle regarding the bets most ripe for manipulation.

title: Dream pairing: How Angel Reese and her new team brought out the best in each other to reach the WNBA Finals - CBS Sports
description: Reese, who could be the first star of her generation to win a WNBA title, has changed her game with the Dream
body:
Reese, who could be the first star of her generation to win a WNBA title, has changed her game with the Dream
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream currently sit just four games away from being crowned WNBA champions. It would be a franchise-first for the Dream, who joined the WNBA in 2008, and make Reese the first star of her generation to lead her team to a title. Things looked very different for both parties not so long ago.This time last year, then-Chicago Sky forward Angel Reese was sitting at home on her couch, watching the Finals from afar after missing the postseason in her first two years in the league. About 700 miles south in Atlanta, the Dream were in soul-searching mode after the winningest regular season in Dream history ended in a postseason flameout.Reese's two years in Chicago had been marked by phenomenal individual play on the court and a sizeable economic impact to the franchise and community, both of which were often overshadowed by poor team play, perplexing roster decisions, coaching instability and front-office mismanagement. By the end of the 2025 season, when Reese gave an ill-advised on-the-record interview to the Chicago Tribune that threw shade on teammates and leadership (and the Sky responded by suspending her for half of a game), it was clear that the two sides were no longer bringing out the best in one another.
        
            
                2026 WNBA Finals predictions: Expert picks for Valkyries vs. Dream as each team seeks first title
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Meanwhile, the Dream's first year under new head coach Karl Smesko had resulted in 15 more wins than their 2024 campaign and a No. 3 seed and home-court advantage in the playoffs, but the end result was the same as it had been the two years prior: A first-round loss, this time at the hands of an injury-plagued Indiana Fever team. The Dream had All-Stars, but no superstars; they were tough, but lacked a competitive fire; they had a strong culture and core, but did not know how to harness any of that when it mattered the most. 
So, when Reese was traded from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream on April 6, the match immediately made sense. Reese needed a fresh start, a steady organization and a talented roster. The Dream needed a winner and a fighter -- not to mention one of the best rebounders and defenders in the game."It felt like the right situation for me, and I felt like I was able to come here and help the team in any way I could. Coaches and a GM that really believe in me was something I was really, really wanting after my first two years," Reese said in her introductory press conference.How the Dream made Reese betterBut what turned the pairing from sensible to sensational was what came next. Smesko knew that the skillset Reese came to town with would make the Dream better instantly. But she lacked in one area that Smesko is famous for valuing -- the ability to shoot from the 3-point line. Due to the condensed offseason schedule, a consequence of the late arrival of the new CBA, Smesko didn't have time to feel Reese out, ease her into his system, to see first-hand if the rumors that had always followed her about being a diva or too distracted by off-court endeavors were true. He had to decide right away how much change she could handle. And so Smesko did what he's always done -- he decided to coach Reese hard. And Reese let him.
Right away, he set out to change her shooting motion and push her to take more shots from the 3-point line. He told her that if she made one more 3-pointer every 25 shots, even that would make a difference in how teams guarded her. And then he put her under duress. There was no time for this growth to happen in private; the season would be starting in a few weeks. She was going to have to try new things, and fail at them, in front of everyone."It's really hard for me to not want to rush success. And Karl told me how patient I had to be with it," Reese recalled after the semifinals, when asked about her improvements from outside the arch.Just a couple of days into training camp, in a new city on a new team with new eyes tracking her every move, the players were doing a 3-point drill when Smesko stopped practice and told Reese that she had to make two 3-pointers in a row, in front of everyone, before practice resumed. Everyone had to stop what they were doing and watch Reese try to succeed at the only part of basketball she hadn't yet mastered. 
"I was upset with him that day for sure because I didn't want to let the team down. I didn't want to feel embarrassed of how long it could have took me to make them," she said. "I think you have to understand -- you're at the W level, and we changed her shot, like, completely, and then we asked her to do it in games. And we talked about it," Smesko said. "We said, 'Before the All Star break, you're still going to shoot these open threes. This is how we want you to shoot it. It's not going to be a good percentage. After the All Star break, it's going to start to get better. By the time we get to the end of the season, it'll start to feel really comfortable.'"So you had to go through all those growing pains, and do that in front of everybody. That's the reason why I had her do it in front of her teammates. You're going to have to get comfortable shooting this ball in front of people, and it's brand new to you. It's not comfortable to you."
Smesko was right about the timeline. Before the All-Star break, Reese shot 12% on 3-pointers. After All-Star break, that improved to 25%. In the playoffs? It has improved to 38.5% and been a huge reason why the Dream have not yet lost a game in this postseason."Now it's so easy. My confidence is through the roof," Reese said. "When I shoot them, it just feels like practice. You have those tough times, and you have those tough conversations. But it's a coach that really believes in you, and he knows he knows what's best. And I'm really thankful for him for being able to help me with my career and help me be better for the team. Because I don't think I would be in this situation and thriving as I am individually without him."It won't be easy vs. ValksThe Dream have a tall task ahead of them this series. The Valkyries have home-court advantage, so Reese and co. will start the series on the road in San Francisco on Saturday, and the best defense in the league. But with Reese, the Dream have found their edge and are on a 10-game winning streak. During that span, they've won in blowouts and in tight games, in shootouts and in scrap-fests. And with the Dream, Reese has found the best basketball of her young career, and a place where she can showcase all of her talents and even add some to the mix. The two were a perfect fit, and have worked together to become even greater than the sum of their parts. 
"Just knowing I belong here," Reese said, when asked why she's flourished in Atlanta. "Knowing coming to Atlanta, how much I wanted to help this team and do whatever it takes, not just to get out of the first round, not to just to get out the semis, but to make it to the Finals and win a championship. And the job is not done. We're definitely happy about where we are right now, but we're not satisfied."

title: How Jaedyn Shaw is keeping Gotham's attack afloat in chase for NWSL Shield - CBS Sports
description: A stingy defense has masked an inefficient offense, but Saturday's showdown against the Spirit will test whether
body:
A stingy defense has masked an inefficient offense, but Saturday's showdown against the Spirit will test whether the regular-season leaders have enough firepower for the postseason
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Is Jaedyn Shaw the one thing keeping Gotham FC's season together? While this may feel like a strange question to pose, for a team that's en route to winning the NWSL Shield for the most points in the regular season, Gotham's stats have been quite odd. As Gotham prepare to travel to face the Washington Spirit on Saturday, it's worth taking a look at those Shield credentials with three games left in the regular season.  Gotham have conceded the fewest goals in the league while also scoring the 12th-most goals of any team. They have the second-best goal difference due to their defensive play, but when looking deeper at the numbers, they aren't clearly the best team in the league; that's likely the San Diego Wave. By the numbers, the team chasing them has the better goal difference and expected goals difference.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Of course, soccer is played on grass and not spreadsheets, but this is important to take note of, with the playoffs around the corner. That xG underperformance on the attacking side of the ball is something that could come back to bite this team, as of the top five scorers this season, four are significantly underperforming their xG. Ester Gonzalez may no longer be with the team, but she was close to hitting her expected numbers with six goals from an xG of 7.85. Sam Kerr has four goals from 9.58 xG, Rose Lavelle has four from 6.26 xG, Jordynn Dudley has four from 5.76 xG, and then there's Shaw. How to watch Washington Spirit vs. NJ/NY Gotham, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS Odds: Washington Spirit +160; Draw +230; NJ/NJ Gotham +155While it was surprising not to see Shaw in the most recent United States women's national team camp facing Spain, Emma Hayes made the point that she wanted Shaw to play consistent minutes with the U-23s rather than come off the bench, given the national team's depth on the wings. That's understandable, but Gotham need Shaw to continue performing at this level, or an attack that is already underperforming will crater on the season. 

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Luckily, there isn't a position that Shaw can't get a shot off from or an area of the pitch that she can't score from. Be it cutting inside from the wing, popping up with a header or just taking a rip from outside the box, she's got you covered. And with so many other stars on this Gotham team, other NWSL sides can't focus on taking away Shaw because then someone else will make them pay.  Despite the inefficiency in attack, the club's defense makes this a strong side, even if it's no longer the true super team Gotham were trying to build in New Jersey. That may even be for the best, as to win the NWSL championship, sides have to be well-rounded and have multiple avenues to create danger, which Gotham have.  That could be enough to win a championship, but if a team can limit Shaw's shots, there are fair questions about what Gotham will do next. Facing the third-placed Washington Spirit will be a good test in that regard, but they're more of a test of Gotham's defense than they are of Gotham's attack. But to win a championship, they'll likely need to go through the Spirit anyway, and with the final set for Audi Field, this is good preparation, making Saturday's clash must-watch TV.

title: Aday Mara's NBA debut in question? Spanish club threatening Thunder rookie's eligibility - CBS Sports
description: Mara played for the club in his native Spain before playing three seasons of college basketball
body:
Mara played for the club in his native Spain before playing three seasons of college basketball
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The organization Aday Mara began his professional basketball career with is publicly challenging his move to the Oklahoma City Thunder. Basket Zaragoza, the Spanish club that Mara played for from 2021-23 before he played college basketball at UCLA and Michigan, released a statement on Friday saying Mara is still under contract for the 2026-27 season and it will oppose him suiting up for the Thunder, who chose him with the 12th pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. In a statement, Zaragoza said it has not received a formal request for Mara's international transfer and would oppose such a request if one is made. The club said it has relayed its position to multiple parties, including the Thunder, the NBA, FIBA and the Spanish Basketball Federation. FIBA does not require an international transfer for players to play in the NCAA, but it does for other professional leagues. Spanish newspaper Heraldo de Aragon reported Friday (via Eurohoops.net) that Zaragoza is seeking a financial settlement:As the local newspaper Heraldo de Aragon reported first his former team claims to hold his playing rights and plans to block any international clearance until a financial settlement regarding his departure is reached. This case had initially progressed to litigation and remains without a legal resolution. Therefore, the club has reportedly warned the NBA, the Thunder, FIBA, and the Spanish Basketball Federation that the 7-foot-3 big needs a formal Letter of Clearance to be eligible to play in the 2026–27 Regular Season.In response, the Thunder said Friday that "no clearance from the Spanish team is required" for Mara to play in the NBA. 
"Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA," a team spokesperson said. The 7-foot-3 Mara left Zaragoza, his hometown club, to begin his college basketball career at UCLA in 2023. He played for the Bruins for two seasons before transferring to Michigan, where he became a crucial cog in the Wolverines' national championship run. Mara was one of the best shot blockers in college basketball and vaulted into a first-round pick, landing with Oklahoma City. Mara, 21, has been one of the stars of the preseason and is expected to play a significant role off the bench for the Thunder this season. In Mara's third preseason game against the Hawks, he played 33 minutes and finished with 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and four blocks.
Oklahoma City opens the 2026-27 season against the San Antonio Spurs on Oct. 20.

        Penn State and Michigan will meet on Saturday in a matchup between two teams already in desperation mode midway through the season. Both began the 2026 season hopeful for the future with a new coach in charge. Six weeks into the season, that hope and optimism have turned into doom and gloom for both programs that enter Week 7 on losing streaks in Big Ten play. The Wolverines began the season with a controversial win before beating Oklahoma in Week 2 for what seemed, at the time, like Kyle Whittingham's first signature win in Ann Arbor. However, successive losses to Iowa and Minnesota, where the offense has looked inept, have raised the temperature under Whittingham just five games into his tenure. The Nittany Lions had a lengthy coaching search before finally bringing in Matt Campbell from Iowa State, and Penn State fans expected a swift return to Big Ten contention. Three consecutive losses to open conference play have already raised questions about Campbell's fit in State College, and he finds himself in desperation mode heading on the road into a hostile environment. 
For years, Penn State vs. Michigan was one of the biggest games of the year in the old Big Ten East. This year, what it lacks in intrigue regarding the College Football Playoff race, it makes up for in what it will tell us about the trajectory of two traditional Big Ten powers. The winner will be able to let out a sigh of relief, while the loser will be staring down a fight just to make it to a bowl game in 2026.   Michigan vs. Penn State: Need to know  Bryce Underwood as a runner: In Michigan's biggest win of the season against Oklahoma, it was Underwood running the ball that was the difference for the Wolverines. He carried the ball 18 times for 87 yards and one touchdown, which was by far his most productive rushing game of the season. The Penn State defense has struggled this season, and both Aidan Chiles and Colton Joseph have rushed for touchdowns against them for Northwestern and Wisconsin. Throwing the ball consistently hasn't been a strength of the Michigan offense, and in a game they desperately need, look for the Wolverines to try and take advantage of Underwood as a runner at times -- especially in red zone opportunities. Can Penn State create explosive plays?: Moving the ball on Michigan's defense consistently is a difficult task, and in both of their losses, it was explosives that led to scores for Minnesota and Iowa. Penn State's offense ranks in the middle of the pack in explosive plays this season, but has not been as dynamic since Koby Howard's injury took away their top downfield threat. If the Nittany Lions are going to score against Michigan, they have to find a way to produce some explosive plays. That doesn't always have to mean on offense. Iowa's first touchdown against Michigan came on a punt return. Minnesota forced three turnovers that led to 13 of their 20 points. Penn State will need a handful of chunk plays from the offense and to create some havoc on defense and special teams if they're going to win this game. 
Special teams, special teams, special teams: This is the kind of game where special teams matter a bit more than usual -- which is to say, this is going to be Big Ten football heritage on display. The punters on both sides need to be sharp and avoid handing the opponent a short field. With points at a premium, field goal opportunities will need to be converted. And with two offenses that can get stuck in the mud, a big return could swing this game one way or the other. Special teams has not been the strength of the Wolverines this season, as they rank 89th in special teams SP+, while Penn State is in the middle of the pack (49th). The team that wins the special teams battle will gain a considerable advantage, and for underdog Penn State in particular, being sharp in the third phase is a must to win on the road. Where to watch Michigan vs. Penn State live  Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET  Location: Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, MichiganTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App  Streaming on Paramount+ Premium
  Michigan vs. Penn State prediction, picks  There is a "stoppable force vs. movable object" situation happening here with the Michigan offense against the Penn State defense, but I'm banking on the home team dictating the tempo here in a classic Big Ten rock fight. Michigan games have finished with fewer than 40 total points four times in five games -- with the lone exception being against lowly UTEP -- and even against a leaky Nittany Lions defense, it's hard to see this Michigan offense being overly explosive. On the other side, the Wolverines are still stout as ever on defense, and this seems destined to be a tense, one-score game late, with both teams struggling to top 20 points.  Pick: Under 42.5SportsLine's proven computer model has simulated every Week 7 college football game 10,000 times. Visit SportsLine now to see the picks, all from the model that's on a 48-40 run on top-rated CFB picks this season.

title: Who is MLB's next superteam? Why Brewers, Yankees, Cubs could rise if Dodgers decline - CBS Sports
description: It was the end of a season and maybe the end of a dynasty. The Los Angeles Dodgers were unceremoniously swept in four games in the NLCS
body:
It was the end of a season and maybe the end of a dynasty. The Los Angeles Dodgers were unceremoniously swept in four games in the NLCS by the Milwaukee Brewers. The Brewers erased an early 4-0 deficit to win Game 4 on Thursday (MIL 6, LAD 4). It is Milwaukee's second-ever pennant and first since 1982. The Dodgers, for the first time since 2023, are going home ringless.     "Extremely proud," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said when asked how he felt about his team's recent run. "It never feels good to lose and not accomplish a goal to win the World Series.  It started back in the early part of February.  I love this team and what we had to go through.  It's one of those things that every night we take the field, people are bringing their best to beat us."     Even with the NLCS loss, the Dodgers are undoubtedly the team of the 2020s thanks to their three World Series titles (2020, 2024-25), and they are the closest thing baseball has had to a "superteam" since the late 1990s/early 2000s New York Yankees. There was an air of invincibility surrounding the Dodgers right up until the Brewers sent them home for the winter.     
        
            
                What's next for the Dodgers? Futures of Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal uncertain after elimination
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Baseball is hard. It's a grueling sport with a long regular season, and an increasingly long postseason subject to more randomness than any other sport. Building a superteam is almost impossible, which makes L.A.'s recent run all the more impressive. Yes, they spent A LOT of money, but so did many other teams, and none came close to this level of success.
Which teams have the best chance to emerge as baseball's next superteam? We can debate exactly what we mean by "superteam" (multiple World Series titles? perennial contention?), but it is one of those things you know it when you see it. Here are our potential superteam tiers.     Tier 1: Powerhouses     The best of the best. The teams that, if they win the World Series next year, no one would bat an eye and consider themselves surprised. These are the teams with the best chance to be baseball's next superteam.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles Dodgers: As poorly as they played in the NLCS, and as old as they looked in the NLCS, there's no reason to think the Dodgers won't enter 2027 as the NL West favorites and on the short list of World Series contenders. They're talented, they're smart, and they have unmatched resources (money and tradeable prospects). A salary cap or stiffer competitive balance tax penalties may rein the Dodgers in a bit, but their player development is so good that I suspect they would continue to dominate the sport anyway.     

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Milwaukee Brewers: They have been baseball's best team the last two seasons and almost their entire core is either signed long-term or under team control with little service time. Milwaukee's farm system is also regarded as one of the game's best, if not the best. Infielder Jesús Made is arguably the top prospect in baseball and he should make his MLB debut in 2027. Small market teams are always at a disadvantage when it comes to putting together dynastic runs because money equals margin of error. The Brewers can't plug a roster hole or paper over a mistake with money the way big spending teams can. Salary cap or no salary cap, the next collective bargaining agreement figures to include increased revenue sharing, which would level the financial playing field somewhat.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Yankees: The Yankees are a metronome. They haven't had a losing season since Wayne's World was in theatres, their "bad" seasons are usually pretty good, and they're in the postseason just about every year. Free agency can be a minefield, but the Yankees tend to nail their biggest signings (Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, etc.), and their player development has improved. The Yankees are here because they give themselves a bite at the apple every season. They're in the postseason every year, and any year could be the year things fall into place for a parade down the Canyon of Heroes.          Tier 2: Perennial contenders     These teams are in the postseason more often and not, and they usually find themselves near the top of the standings. They're all just a few breaks and fortunate bounces away from superteam status.     

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta Braves: Other than an injury-plagued 2025 season, the Braves have been to the postseason every year since 2018. They have a prime-aged core on the position player side (Ronald Acuña Jr., Drake Baldwin, Matt Olson, etc.) and the ageless Chris Sale fronting the rotation. The Braves have been held back by depth issues the last few years, however, which prevents them from moving up into Tier 1. They looked like a potential dynasty following their 2021 World Series win. That's a pretty good reminder of how hard it is to win a championship and stay championship-caliber in this game.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Boston Red Sox: The Red Sox must figure out how to break through the ceiling they've hit the last two years (losing the Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium), but gosh, what a core. Roman Anthony, Garrett Crochet, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Payton Tolle are an enviable quartet to build around, and there's a strong supporting cast in place. The Red Sox are one or two big bats away from being a serious problem for the rest of the American League. Even without that big bat(s), they're good enough to reach the postseason and capable of going on a run.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chicago Cubs: They have some heavy lifting ahead of them this offseason, given the state of the rotation and the fact that both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) are free agents. When you start your roster with Pete Crow-Armstrong, though, and have a supporting cast that includes Alex Bregman, Michael Busch and Nico Hoerner, you're about 80% of the way to World Series contention. The Cubs are stuck playing in the same division as the Brewers and that makes life challenging, but in no way does it doom them.      

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cleveland Guardians: Yes, they play in a crummy division, but the Guardians win that crummy division every year and work their way into the postseason. That's more than half the battle when it comes to establishing yourself as a superteam. Cleveland will never run high payrolls, which lessens their margin of error, though the upcoming collective bargaining agreement could improve things for tiny payroll teams. Bottom line, the Guardians keep pumping out quality pitching, and when you do that, you have a chance to win a lot of ballgames.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia Phillies: The Phillies are getting long in the tooth and they're closer to the end of their World Series window than the beginning, but that window is still open. It will remain open as long as they have Jesús Luzardo and Cristopher Sánchez leading the rotation, and Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber anchoring the middle of the lineup. You have to squint to see a potential superteam here, yes, though the foundation of a World Series-contending roster is in place. Improve the supporting cast and the Phillies are right there with any team.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Diego Padres: I am curious to see how the Padres approach their first offseason under their new ownership. José Feliciano and Kwanza Jones, the new owners, insist they will spend to keep the team in contention. OK, so why shouldn't the Padres be in on Tarik Skubal on Day 1 of the offseason then? The Padres have to figure things out on the pitching side, for sure. They badly need more depth. They do have a strong blend of 20-somethings (Jackson Merrill, Ethan Salas, Fernando Tatis Jr.) and veterans (Manny Machado) to build around, though.     

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tampa Bay Rays: Tampa's status as a perennial contender is a wee bit overstated (this is their first postseason appearance since 2023), but they are inarguably one of the smartest teams in baseball, and they have a capital-S Superstar in Junior Caminero. Also, they have a new ballpark coming in the next few years, one that will be located in Tampa rather than St. Petersburg. That should boost revenues and thus payroll, and improve their World Series chances.          Tier 3: You gotta show me something     This tier is reserved for teams that should have been better than they were in 2026. These teams could be on the cusp of superteam status a year from now, but right now, they're all well short for one reason or another.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Mets: The Brewers having the success they've had while the Mets have authored back-to-back disaster seasons begs the question: Is POBO David Stearns really all he's cracked up to be? The silver lining of their lost 2026 season is that several young players emerged as long-term building blocks, most notably Carson Benge and Nolan McLean. Those two, plus Juan Soto, who will turn only 28 later this month, are the makings of a championship-caliber core, plus owner Steve Cohen is very willing to spend. Are the Mets a potential superteam? Yes. Have they earned the benefit of the doubt? Absolutely not.     

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seattle Mariners: Expectations were sky high coming into the season and then the Mariners fell flat and finished five games back in what was arguably the worst division in baseball history. More distressingly, franchise players Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodríguez took big steps back. It feels like the range of potential outcomes for the 2027 Mariners is massive. You could tell me they'll win 102 games and storm to the World Series, and I'd believe it. You could also tell me they'll stumble to 75 wins and Rodriguez's name will pop up in trade rumors, and I'd believe that too.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Toronto Blue Jays: Last year, the Blue Jays came as close to winning the World Series as you can without actually winning the World Series. If Vladimir Guerrero Jr. continues to be this moving forward, that's an enormous problem and puts a serious dent in Toronto's World Series hopes. I'm willing to give Guerrero and the Blue Jays some benefit of the doubt and assume 2026 is not their new normal, but not so much that I'll move them into Tier 2. They have won a postseason series in just one of the last 10 seasons, after all.          Tier 4: Up-and-comers     At best, these teams are a year away from being a year away from possible superteam status, but they are arrow-up organizations rapidly approaching contention. If they were a stock, I'd say buy buy buy.     

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chicago White Sox: I thought the White Sox were a year away entering 2026. Instead, so many of their young players took a step forward at once, and they were able to contend for the AL Central title. Making the jump from rebuilder to contender is the easy part. The hard part is staying in contention. To do that, the White Sox must come up with more pitching, and we need to see some more commitment (i.e. raise payroll) from owner Jerry Reinsdorf, who treats the ChiSox as the smallest big market team in baseball.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    St. Louis Cardinals: The transition from John Mozeliak to new POBO Chaim Bloom is complete, and now the farm system and player development apparatus is on the rise. The Cardinals have several building-block position players in place (Masyn Winn, Jordan Walker, JJ Wetherholt) with more on the way (Jesús Báez, Rainiel Rodriguez, etc.). Now the pitching must catch up to the position player side of things, and pitchers are wizards these days. Anyone could break out at any moment. The Cardinals are on the cusp of a return to sustained contention.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington Nationals: The new front office, led by POBO Paul Toboni, is getting rave reviews. The results are already showing up on the field, too. CJ Abrams, Cade Cavalli, and Jacob Young all made leaps this season. They turned low-cost pickups Foster Griffin and Curtis Mead into a bounty of young players at the trade deadline. The farm system is robust. The Nationals are in a brutal division, but the third wild card spot is very forgiving. All indications are that they will compete for one of them soon, and the NL East title not long after that.

title: Can the Broncos win a Super Bowl with Bo Nix? His stats tell a troubling story - CBS Sports
description: Bo Nix is 28-12 through his first 40 NFL starts, more victories than John Elway and Peyton Manning had over that same stretch. Among act
body:
Bo Nix is 28-12 through his first 40 NFL starts, more victories than John Elway and Peyton Manning had over that same stretch. Among active quarterbacks, only Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson had better records at this point in their careers.There's just one problem: Nix is directing one of the NFL's least productive offenses, and his individual numbers are getting worse. So what exactly should we make of all that success?Thursday night's 17-14 overtime victory against Seattle might have been the most extreme example yet. Denver managed 168 yards of offense, averaged 2.9 yards per play and gained a grand total of 38 yards on 25 plays after halftime. Nix finished with 107 passing yards, averaging exactly four yards per attempt.Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick wasn't nearly as forgiving. During Amazon's postgame show, he ripped Nix's performance, saying, "He's not playing competitive football right now," and later calling it "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position." 
So, yeah … the Broncos improved to 4-2 and extended their streak of one-score victories to 14 games. Their defense dominated for long stretches, forcing turnovers and capitalizing on Seattle's mistakes. And it's not a stretch to suggest they accomplished all this in spite of, not because of Bo Nix.Denver has a defense capable of carrying this team to the Super Bowl. But if Nix can't give the Broncos more than he has through the first six games, none of that matters. Put more bluntly: How much longer are they willing to wait for him to figure it out?What Nix's first 39 starts actually tell usIt's easy to look at Nix's 2026 numbers, throw your hands up and conclude that he's suddenly fallen apart. The third-year quarterback has undoubtedly gotten worse this season, but some of the problems have been there all along.
Nix threw 29 touchdowns and 12 interceptions as a rookie in 2024 and helped Denver reach the playoffs. He followed that with another winning season, and through his first 39 starts, he'd thrown 60 touchdowns, completed 64.2% of his passes and piled up 8,648 passing yards.Those aren't bad numbers, and Nix, at times, has looked comfortable running Sean Payton's offense. Enough to give Denver reason to believe it had found its long-term answer. But look a little deeper, and the picture starts to change.Nix's efficiency -- how consistently he moves the ball, creates big plays and avoids negative ones -- doesn't quite match his impressive record, according to TruMedia. To put that into perspective, we compared him to a sample of 74 other quarterbacks drafted since 2008, looking at how each performed through his first 39 starts over his first three NFL seasons.
NixRankEPA/dropback+0.0530thSuccess rate43.4%40thYards/attempt6.459thAdjusted yards/attempt7.073rdExplosive plays/dropback7.4%45thSack rate3.7%1stPressure-to-sack rate11.2%75th (best)Nix excelled at avoiding sacks, getting the ball out quickly and keeping Denver out of trouble. But there was a tradeoff: He wasn't making nearly enough big plays through the air, and his 6.4 yards per attempt ranked 59th among the 75 quarterbacks in our sample.In other words, Nix was good at avoiding mistakes, but not nearly as good at making plays that could change a game. And through six games in 2026, even that formula has started to fall apart.The warning signs are getting harder to ignoreNix isn't just throwing shorter passes. He's taking fewer chances downfield, making more turnover-worthy plays and struggling to move the offense. And when he does drop back, he's getting less out of those opportunities than at any point in his career.Consider how his numbers have changed since his rookie season.202420252026Yards/attempt6.76.45.6EPA/dropback+0.05+0.11-0.12Average depth of target7.88.06.3Big-time throw rate3.5%4.8%2.4%Turnover-worthy play rate1.9%2.8%5.0%Accuracy percentage76.7%75.6%74.7%Pressure-to-sack rate13.3%10.1%10.1%There was genuine progress in 2025. Nix's EPA per dropback increased, his big-time throw rate improved and he did a better job of avoiding sacks when pressured. That's meaningful, and it offers at least some evidence that he was improving.But through six games in 2026, those gains have largely disappeared. His big-time throw rate has been cut in half, his turnover-worthy play rate has nearly doubled from last season and his EPA per dropback has turned negative.And while his accuracy rate has remained stable, he's generating fewer first downs, explosive plays and touchdowns. And he's putting the ball in harm's way more often.There's also the ankle injury to consider. Nix underwent surgery after fracturing his right ankle in January's playoff win over Buffalo, but he has repeatedly insisted he's fully healthy. Asked directly after Denver's Week 4 loss to San Francisco whether the injury was affecting his play, he offered a one-word answer: "No." It's certainly fair to wonder, based on what we've all witnessed this season, if that's not entirely true.  There's also the fact that Payton has commandeered play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, hoping to jump-start an offense that had struggled through its first four games.So far, it hasn't helped. Denver managed just 224 yards against the Chargers in Week 5 and 168 against Seattle, and the Broncos now rank 31st in yards per game and last in yards per play. Payton helped Nix develop over his first two seasons, but the last two weeks have only raised more questions about whether he'll ever become the quarterback Denver envisioned when they drafted him.How Nix compares to the other QBs in that 2024 draft classNix was the 12th overall pick, and the sixth quarterback taken in the 2024 NFL Draft, behind Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye, Michael Penix Jr. and JJ McCarthy.Some two-and-a-half seasons later, how does Nix stack up against his classmates? Maye helped lead the Patriots to the Super Bowl in Year 2, while Daniels took Washington to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie. Williams made significant strides under Ben Johnson in 2025, leading Chicago to a division title and a playoff victory, and Penix has been surprisingly impressive this season. Even with injuries complicating the comparisons, there's enough evidence to suggest every quarterback in this class not named Nix or McCarthy is developing into the player their teams envisioned. 2024 first-round QB class: NFL passing production, 2024-26QuarterbackGamesYPAEPA/dropbackTD-INTDrake Maye358.1+0.1754-25Jayden Daniels277.1+0.1436-12Michael Penix Jr.177.6+0.1115-7Bo Nix406.4+0.0560-26Caleb Williams366.7+0.0549-14J.J. McCarthy106.7-0.1011-12Nix has started more games than anyone in the group, and unlike several of his classmates, he's had the same coach and offensive system since arriving in the NFL. That stability should have helped his development, and for a while, it appeared to. But through six games in '26, Nix is heading in the wrong direction.That doesn't mean Denver should give up and move on. But after 40 starts, his struggles raise a bigger question: How much longer should the Broncos expect to wait for a breakthrough?What history says about young QBs who struggle this longSo what happens to quarterbacks whose numbers look like Nix's after some 40 starts? Do they figure it out, or is three seasons enough to know what you have?The good news for Denver is that some quarterbacks do turn things around. The bad news? Most don't suddenly become stars. There's a big difference between improving enough to keep your job and becoming the guy who can carry a team to the Super Bowl.We used TruMedia data to look at 24 quarterbacks whose early-career efficiency resembled Nix's, then compared their first 39 starts with their next 21. Nine improved their EPA per dropback by at least 0.05. But just four reached +0.10 or better, and as it turns out, even that didn't guarantee long-term success.What happened to quarterbacks who started their careers like Bo Nix?QuarterbackFirst 39 startsStarts 40-60Starts 61-80Josh Allen+0.06+0.15+0.21Dak Prescott+0.06+0.18+0.12Tua Tagovailoa+0.05+0.17-0.02Jared Goff+0.06+0.10-0.10Baker Mayfield+0.01+0.06-0.08Derek Carr0.00+0.06-0.02Andy Dalton+0.01+0.03+0.15Blake Bortles-0.03+0.05-0.09Mitchell Trubisky+0.01-0.02—Mark Sanchez0.00-0.13—Josh Allen and Dak Prescott give Denver some hope. Both started with numbers similar to Nix's, took major steps forward over their next 21 starts and continued to produce at a high level over the following 20 games. Andy Dalton, stylistically a much closer comp to Nix than Allen or Prescott, needed a little longer, making his biggest leap between starts 61 and 80.Others followed a different path. Tua Tagovailoa, Jared Goff and Baker Mayfield initially improved, only to see their numbers fall off during the next 20 starts. Derek Carr and Blake Bortles also made gains before regressing, while Mitch Trubisky and Mark Sanchez, both top-5 picks in their respective draft classes, never made much progress. Of course, Goff and Mayfield eventually turned their careers around, which shows that development is rarely linear.And there's another catch: Our comparison only includes quarterbacks who had at least 300 dropbacks after their first 39 starts. Some struggling quarterbacks never got that opportunity because their teams moved on. Put another way: The odds of a turnaround may be even worse than our numbers suggest.So where does that leave Nix? He's done enough to keep his starting job for now, but his performance has gotten worse in Year 3.  History offers some hope that he can still figure things out, but it also gives Payton and general manager George Paton good reason to wonder how much longer they should wait.How much longer can Denver afford to wait?Under ordinary circumstances, the answer might be straightforward. Nix is still young. He's won a lot of games, and the Broncos have invested heavily in his development. Give him more time and see where things go.But Denver isn't in an ordinary situation.
The Broncos have a defense capable of keeping them in every game. They have a coach who has already won a Super Bowl, and they've built a team that doesn't need its quarterback to throw for 350 yards every week.What they need is an offense that can consistently move the ball. Right now, it's nonexistent.And that's what makes the coming offseason potentially so important. Nix is under contract through 2027, with Denver holding a fifth-year option for 2028. The Broncos don't have to decide his long-term future just yet, but they can't afford to waste a championship-caliber defense waiting for him to develop.There's no guarantee this defense will be this dominant in 2027, never mind 2-3 years down the road; injuries happen, contracts expire, players and units regress, and championship windows can slam shut.That doesn't mean Denver needs to move on from Nix, but they would be foolish not to start considering other options. Nix can change the conversation over the next few months. But Payton and Paton also need to prepare for the possibility that the quarterback they have isn't the one they need to win a Super Bowl.That could mean using a 2027 draft pick on a quarterback or bringing in legitimate veteran competition. Neither would necessarily mean giving up on Nix – J.J. McCarthy might like a word, I know. Either way,  it would give Denver another option if his struggles continue.(By the way, I've documented – extensively, some might say – Arch Manning's struggles this season for Texas. He wasn't a first-round pick in my latest mock draft, or the latest mock draft we did on the "With the First Pick" podcast … that said, imagine if Payton got his hands on him. Just something to think about.)The Broncos have spent two-plus seasons waiting for Nix to grow into a franchise quarterback. They can afford to give him more time, but they can't afford to squander a Super Bowl window hoping for a breakthrough that may never come.

        One of college football's great rivalries takes center stage on Saturday night when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State for their traditional October clash. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications, though this season those conversations are focused far more on Miami, which finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender.
  Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know  A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation.   Florida State struggling against top teams: While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami.  No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026: The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest) was decided by less than 28 points.

TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks  Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. Pick: Miami -21

The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents.Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama.While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary.The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020.
  Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know  Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time.Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon. Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop, and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver.Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss.

Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. Pick: Alabama -8.5

        Texas coach Steve Sarkisian is sticking to his guns — in this case, his play-calling — and believes the scrutiny of Arch Manning is unjustified heading into Saturday's game against Florida. Manning's inconsistency has kept the Longhorns' offense largely out of rhythm this season, a critique he'll try to correct against the SEC's worst defense. After a loss to rival Oklahoma sent the Longhorns falling six spots in the AP Poll, Texas is hoping to use the tailspinning Gators as their punching bag to stay in the College Football Playoff picture. Florida has lost back-to-back SEC games in blowout fashion, tumbling out of the national rankings without a clear solution to stop the hemorrhaging. Sumrall said progress is sometimes "dysfunctional" and agreed with some of the booing he experienced on the sideline of last week's loss to South Carolina. The Gators struggled to block Gamecocks edge Dylan Stewart and now must endure the athleticism of Colin Simmons, who leads college football with 9.5 sacks. Simmons collected five sacks during a win at Tennessee last month and is the runaway favorite to win the SEC's Defensive Player of the Year honor.

The Fighting Irish cruised to a 6-0 win, only playing one game within two scores to rank among the best teams in the country. Last week, they obliterated Stanford 58-7 behind 181 yards rushing from Jonaz WaltonBYU's also been dominant during a 5-0 start, with four wins coming by multiple scores. They have an impressive early-season win over Arizona, and held Iowa State to fewer than 100 yards until late in the fourth quarter. The Cougars are fresh off a Big 12 title game appearance only three years after joining the power conferences. The Fighting Irish and Cougars have played seven times in history, with Notre Dame holding a 5-2 advantage. Notre Dame has won all four matchups since 2005, including a 28-20 win during the Shamrock Classic in Las Vegas in 2022. Notre Dame vs. BYU: Need to know  Super CJ: Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr is off to a blazing start to his second season as a starter, ranking among the most efficient passers in the country. Carr is completing 71% of his passes, averaging 9.6 yards per attempt and has thrown 16 touchdowns to one interception. Wide receivers Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert are neck-and-neck with more than 375 yards receiving each. Star down: BYU running back LJ Martin will miss the matchup against Notre Dame, dealing a significant blow to the Cougars' offense. The senior from El Paso posted nearly 1,600 all-purpose yards last year, ranking among the most impressive rushers in the nation. With Martin sidelined last week, the onus fell on quarterback Bear Bachmeier, who ran for 109 yards in the win. No running back cleared 21 yards on the ground, bringing up the significant question of how the Cougars can generate offense against the elite Notre Dame defensive front.

        The 100th all-time meeting between Ohio State and Indiana should be a good one. The No. 5 Hoosiers host the fourth-ranked Buckeys with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to Indianapolis.The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss).Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith, who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category.This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State.
Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to knowAnnual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands.Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year.Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical.

Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time.         Captain Canada comes home with his self-anointed "Maple Leaf Militia." Mike Malott makes his seventh straight start in Canada on Saturday, headlining in his home nation in back-to-back fights. This time, he wants Joaquin Buckley's No. 10 welterweight ranking at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton.This is make-or-break for Buckley (21-8). "New Mansa," a reference to the historical Mali Empire ruler Mansa Musa, seemed to be on his own conquest after he knocked out former title challengers Stephen Thompson and Colby Covington. Buckley has always shown potential; look no further than his iconic spinning back kick KO against Impa Kasanganay. Unfortunately, dominant grappling losses to Kamaru Usman and Sean Brady completely halted his momentum. His confidence remains intact, even if outside belief is dwindling, as he defends his spot in the welterweight Top 10 this weekend."I thought I was very, very, very prepared for Sean Brady. I thought I was, to be honest, and Sean Brady came in and did his job," Buckley told CBS Sports. "But I can't be concerned about what the other man is going to do. I just have to put myself in a position where I'm always on the offensive. And a great offense is a great defense."Malott (14-2-1) has a very unique role in the UFC ecosystem. He's essentially become the North Star for a Great White North sorely in need of it. It's been nearly four years since Malott has fought outside of Canada. His first main event, which took place in April, saw him knock out and retire longtime contender Gilbert Burns. If Malott can stop Buckley, who is two years younger than him despite being the UFC veteran, he'll be on a collision course with the division's top names.
"There are definitely things we saw in studying him that we believe we can take advantage of in all aspects of fighting," Malott told CBS Sports. "I don't love scripting a fight. I'm more focused on preparation than prediction... Man, fighting is chaos. Preparing the skills for whatever could arise, going in there and jamming, feeling it out, and taking where I feel right. I've done that pretty much every time, and it's worked well for me." The co-main event has even more immediate title implications than the main event. The women's flyweight division is radically changing after Valentina Shevchenko vacated her title earlier this year due to injury. Natalia Silva defeated Wang Cong to become the new champion at UFC 332. That ticks off Erin Blanchfield. Long, labeled a future title challenger, Blanchfield believes she deserved the opportunity that ultimately went to Cong. A statement win against Jasmine Jasudavicius is paramount this weekend, especially with Alexa Grasso's resurgence and Shevchenko's inevitable return.It's Canada vs. the world at UFC Fight Night. All but one of the 13 fights scheduled feature a Canadian in one corner. Among them is Mandel Nallo, a vicious striker who was putting a hurting on Jai Herbert before getting caught. The biggest betting favorite among the home athletes is Melissa Croden (-300), defending her No. 15 women's bantamweight ranking.
Let's take a look at the rest of the fight card with the latest odds from DraftKings before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.UFC Fight Night card, oddsFavoriteUnderdogWeightclassMike Malott -135Joaquin Buckley +114WelterweightErin Blanchfield -325Jasmine Jasudavicius +260Women's flyweightCristian Perez -340Kyle Nelson +270LightweightKyle Daukaus -185Marc-Andre Barriault +154MiddleweightLouis Jourdain -180Timmy Cuamba +150BantamweightMandel Nallo -285  Nate Landwehr +230  LightweightUFC Fight Night viewing informationDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Start time: 8 p.m. ET (Main card), 5 p.m. (Prelims)Location: Rogers Place -- Edmonton, CanadaTV Channel: Paramount+ (subscribe now for as low as $8.99 per month)          PredictionJoaquin Buckley vs. Mike Malott: There are serious questions about Buckley's defensive grappling. That cannot be denied. But I'm not sure Malott, despite his grappling trophies, can capitalize as Usman and Brady did. Buckley showed great wrestling defense against Colby Covington and has been competing in Real American Freestyle. He hasn't had a good run there, but he's diligently patching that hole. It's more complicated on the feet. I believe Malott, the former striking coach at Team Alpha Male, is the better technical striker even though he lacks Buckley's flashiness. Malott will have early success, but it's the late game that worries me. Malott's loss to Neil Magny taught him to pace himself. How that translates to five rounds, however, is still a mystery. By contrast, we've seen Buckley winging punches at Usman in the fifth round of an exhausting fight. Buckley could start taking over partway through Round 3, if the fight lasts that long. Buckley's chin is far from foolproof, but his defensive sensibilities have improved drastically over the years. If this fight goes long, which I'm predicting it will, Buckley should sneak ahead and even stop an exhausted Malott. Pick: Buckley via KO, Round 4.
